metallicity.note: Literature [Fe/H]=-0.25 is an exact tie in grid-step distance between the two nearest available CK04 metallicities, 0.0 (ckp00) and -0.5 (ckm05) -- both are 0.25 dex away. With the full 608-file CK04 grid: both slices were tested empirically with fit_photometry() (script: scripts/ck04_metallicity_rerun_check.py). At metallicity=0.0 (current, kept): reduced chi2=0.112, radius rel. err. <=0.75%, Teff rel. err. <=6.37%. At metallicity=-0.5 (tested alternative): reduced chi2=0.164 (worse), radius rel. err. <=0.23% (better), Teff rel. err. <=6.37% (primary_temperature pins at the grid's 5000K lower edge in BOTH cases -- the same near-twin-component-temperature degeneracy already documented in docs/guide/binary_sed.md, not affected by this choice). Kept at 0.0 on the reduced-chi2 tiebreaker (the standard overall fit-quality metric); the alternative is documented here rather than silently discarded, since the tie means either choice is scientifically defensible.

primary_logg.note: Derived from literature M=0.91 Msun, R=0.832 Rsun via logg=4.4377+log10(M)-2log10(R); not stated directly in the source paper (Table 5 gives only a system-wide range, ~4.37-4.80).

secondary_logg.note: Derived from literature M=0.85 Msun, R=0.783 Rsun the same way.

atmosphere_grid_note: Common grid for all four SED benchmarks since v0.2.0: CK04 solar metallicity, 3500-10000 K (27 models). The earlier per-system grids of 3-4 nodes bracketing the published temperatures bounded the temperature agreement by construction (scripts/sed_wide_grid.py).

measurements.note: Abushattal et al. (2025) Table 4 entire-system magnitude. That table is the paper's own synthetic photometry of its adopted solution, not observed photometry, so the 0.30 mag uncertainty is a tolerance, not a measurement error. At the adopted distance the table's V magnitudes are 0.13-0.40 mag fainter (system-dependent) than the same paper's Table 5 absolute magnitudes imply (validation/results/published_params_photometry.json); with the distance fixed and the radii held near their published values by the prior, the fit absorbs that offset mainly by lowering both temperatures. Magnitudes are on the standard Johnson, Stromgren uvby and Tycho systems; PySeshat's zero points are converted to those systems since 0.2.0 (pyseshat.photometry.calibration).

radius_prior_note: Radius is FREED (not held fixed) alongside Teff1/Teff2, with a Gaussian prior (see validation/benchmark_runner.py, _RADIUS_PRIOR_RELATIVE_SIGMA) tying each component's radius to this system's literature value (literature_component_parameters) with an assumed 10% relative sigma -- the source paper's Table 5 gives no formal radius uncertainty for any of the four systems. Freeing the radii with NO constraint at all exposes a genuine, band-count-independent physical degeneracy of unresolved-binary photometric SED fitting -- an unresolved combined-light SED alone cannot uniquely separate two stars' individual (Teff, R) pairs, no matter how many passbands are added, because each star's broadband flux depends on Teff and R only through the combination R^2*Teff^4-ish integrated over the passband. A Gaussian prior is the appropriate middle ground: it keeps the fit on the physical branch of that degeneracy while still letting the data pull radius away from its literature value if it genuinely disagrees, rather than freezing it outright.
ebv_note: E(B-V) held at 0 (system within 75 pc). With E(B-V) free, reddened solutions up to ~8500 K fit the combined light within dchi2 < 1 (validation/results/sed_wide_grid*.json).
magnitude_difference_note: m_B - m_A in Johnson V from the component magnitudes of Abushattal et al. (2025) Table 4 (the same table as the combined photometry); 0.09 mag is the value stated as input for HD 130669. Uncertainty 0.05 mag assumed (typical of speckle Delta m). Without it, the component temperatures of near-twin pairs can be exchanged (validation/results/sed_wide_grid_ebv0.json).
